column1: # The drivers and blocks that atoom releases as executables: one row for each, and the one place that says which executables are built, archived, packaged and
# put in an image (docs/packages.md). Columns, separated by a tab:
#   id          <port>-<driver> for a driver, block-<name> for the thin main of a block (blocks/<name>): the name of the tarball
#               (atoom-<id>_<version>_<os>_<arch>.tar.gz), of the executable in the package and the image (/usr/bin/atoom-<id>), of the image
#               (ghcr.io/truvity/atoom-<id>); the package is atoom-driver-<id> for a driver and atoom-<id> (atoom-block-<name>) for a block
#   lang        go or rust
#   dir         the directory of the driver or the block in the repository
#   target      go: the main package, below dir (the Go module); rust: <cargo package>:<bin name>
#   build       portable: Go with CGO off, Rust through cargo-zigbuild to static musl, cross-compiled for both architectures;
#               native:<go build tag>: Go with cgo, built on a host of each architecture in an Ubuntu 22.04 userland (tools/release/native-build.sh)
#   os          the operating systems of the tarballs (linux; darwin for pure Go); the packages and images are Linux
#   deb_dep, rpm_dep, deb_rec, rpm_rec   the runtime dependencies and recommendations of the packages, comma separated; - for none
#   summary     the one line of the package, the image and the tarball
# `tools/release/check-table.sh` holds this file to the tree: a thin main that is neither here nor in its exceptions fails the check.
key-software
column11: The software key driver of the key port: keys held in files, served on a UNIX socket
